item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Hurricane Polo barrels towards Baja California region of Mexico
item.description:
Area’s second-most intense hurricane on record being fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters

Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system in a Pacific hurricane season that has been notably active in recent months. On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for the system to maintain its considerable strength.

Polo is expected to turn towards the west-north-west, before taking a more north-westerly trajectory on Saturday. It has maximum sustained winds of around 150mph, with even stronger gusts occurring within the most intense parts of the hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend outward for approximately 40 miles from the centre, while tropical storm-force winds reach as far as 125 miles. These powerful winds, combined with torrential rainfall and dangerous seas, could have significant impacts. Although some fluctuations in intensity are possible over the coming days, Polo is expected to remain powerful as it tracks north-westwards.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Report: ICC deputy prosecutor says court has insulated itself against US sanctions
item.description:
Report: ICC deputy prosecutor says court has insulated itself against US sanctions

Deputy prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, Nazhat Shameem Khan, has said that the court has insulated itself against potential court-wide sanctions from the US, according to the Financial Times.

“The law must prevail over power,” Khan told the newspaper.

The prospect of more US sanctions comes after Trump told the UN General Assembly this week that the ICC was “out of control” and an “evil group of people”, calling on the court’s member states to resign from the institution immediately.

His attacks on the court have increased in his second term after the ICC issued an arrest warrant in 2024 against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant for alleged war crimes in Gaza.

“I’m not waiting. I think the lesson in resilience, this lesson in dedication, in maintaining the work of the court, that’s now. That’s something we must do now,” Khan said.

The court has overhauled its systems, shifting its office software from Microsoft to Germany’s openDesk, and finding workarounds on banking and health insurance, she said. The court declined to elaborate on the workarounds to protect their effectiveness.

The tribunal has also been paying employees months in advance to mitigate any disruption to its payroll.

Khan said some individuals at the court who have been placed under sanctions had experienced “over-compliance” by institutions and had to “meander around sanctions to be able to survive them”.

ICC staff were told last year that more than 90 per cent of the court’s processes at that time relied on US technology systems.

Khan said that while the provisions were still a “work in progress”, the court had taken considerable strides to minimise the impact of any restrictions.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Report: UAE-owned Manchester City found guilty of financial rules breach
item.description:
Report: UAE-owned Manchester City found guilty of financial rules breach

Submitted by MEE staff on Sat, 09/26/2026 - 01:50
The club is looking at points deduction serious enough to relegate them, or even expulsion from the Premier League in the worst-case scenario
Under the ownership of Sheikh Mansour, City have become the dominant force in English soccer. (AFP)
Off

The UAE-owned Manchester City have been found guilty on all but one of the 115 financial charges it faces for breaching financial rules, the Athletic reported, an outcome that could send shockwaves through English soccer and potentially sour UAE-UK relations.

City was charged by the Premier League in 2023 following an investigation into alleged breaches between 2009 and 2018. 

It was accused of failing to provide accurate financial information and details of payments to players and coaches, as well as breaches of financial sustainability rules. 

According to the Athletic, no sanction had yet been decided and that City is set to appeal. But BBC reported that the punishment decided by the panel will be released before any appeal is completed.

If found guilty, City are looking at a points deduction serious enough to relegate them, large fines or, in the worst-case scenario, even expulsion from the Premier League.

The club won three Premier League titles, three League Cups and the FA Cup during the time in question, which ran up to 2017-18. 

UAE-owned Manchester City’s ban from European football overturned
Read More »

On Friday, the Athletic reported that Premier League clubs are planning legal action and several teams mobilised leading lawyers to ascertain what they may be eligible to claim for, and a number of clubs are talking to each other about this. 

Legal firms have been contacting clubs to inform them that they would be in a position to claim compensation if Manchester City are found to have breached the Premier League’s rules, the report said.

The club is owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, deputy prime minister and vice president of the UAE, who bought the club in September 2008 for around £200 million. 

Under the ownership of Sheikh Mansour, City have become the dominant force in English soccer. It has won eight Premier League titles, four FA Cups, seven League Cups and one Champions League in the past 15 years. 

Investigations into Manchester City’s financial breaches came after leaked documents published by German outlet Der Spiegel back in 2018. Emails purportedly exchanged between top City executives showed the club had inflated sponsorship revenue from Abu Dhabi state-controlled airline Etihad and telecoms firm Etisalat by disguising direct investment from Mansour’s Abu Dhabi United Group as income.

‘Negative outcome could damage UAE-UK relations’

Bloomberg reported last month that UAE officials cautioned that a negative outcome could damage improved relations with the UK.

Manchester City has evolved into the flagship investment since being taken over in 2008 by Sheikh Mansour, both in the UK and UAE.

Branded Manchester City residences are being developed in Abu Dhabi, accompanied by a Manchester City Training Academy featuring a “Match Day Terrace” for fans to watch matches on a big screen. Additionally, a dedicated Manchester City retail store is located on Yas Island. 

UK criticises Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour for meeting Syrian president
Read More »

The UAE had also invested billions of dollars into rejuvenating a downtrodden part of Manchester, with joint ventures in social housing and improvements to sports facilities.

Burnham was Manchester mayor for nine years before taking over as British prime minister last month. Sheikh Mansour’s private investment vehicle, Abu Dhabi United Group, is a prominent investor in urban regeneration.

During his tenure as Manchester mayor, Burnham praised Manchester City’s owners and the funding they have put into the east of the city.

Burnham held his first phone call with United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Sheikh Mansour’s brother, in late July, as he seeks to broaden the UK’s investment appeal to wealthy allies like the UAE.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Ed Sheeran shows at stadium owned by pro-Israel Robert Kraft cancelled
item.description:
Ed Sheeran shows at stadium owned by pro-Israel Robert Kraft cancelled

Submitted by MEE and agencies on Sat, 09/26/2026 - 03:04
Concert promoter Messina Touring said the concerts were called off due to severe weather warnings
Ed Sheeran's US tour been overshadowed by widespread international backlash for dropping his pro-Palestinian support act, Macklemore. (AFP)
Off

Ed Sheeran's weekend shows at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, the venue owned by pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft who had pushed for Macklemore's removal from the tour over his pro-Palestinian remarks, have been cancelled.

"Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium," concert promoter Messina Touring posted on Instagram on Friday morning. 

"The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as a top priority."

Messina Touring said that any tickets purchased through Ticketmaster would be automatically refunded. Outside of Ticketmaster, refunds are currently available at the point of purchase. 

The British pop icon’s American tour has been overshadowed by widespread international backlash for dropping his pro-Palestinian support act, Macklemore. 

In Philadelphia, where he performed for the first time since Macklemore was taken off the tour, Sheeran apologised to fans and said that what Israel is doing in Gaza is "unjustifiable". 

"I've had to take and make difficult decisions, and I am making mistakes, and I'm so, so sorry," Sheeran told his audience.

All supporting acts quit Ed Sheeran tour in protest of Macklemore’s removal
Read More »

Macklemore was to open for Sheeran, but Kraft had threatened to cancel Sheeran's stadium concerts if he stayed, and lobbied other stadium owners to join him in applying pressure.

In his own statement, Kraft did not deny that he had corralled other wealthy stadium owners to threaten Sheeran and silence Macklemore.

He said his decision was based on Macklemore’s “recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey… that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.”

“I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts,” added Kraft, saying that his goal was “peace for all people, an end to suffering and an end to all hate.”

At the start of the concert at Lincoln Financial Field, Sheeran called Israel's war on Gaza "catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate".

According to US media reports, the start time of Sheeran's concert was pushed back by two and a half hours because of the withdrawal of all the opening acts, and Sheeran performed solo.

Macklemore to begin 'Free Palestine' concert next month

On Thursday, Macklemore announced he would headline his own "Free Palestine" concert tour that will start next month.

The tour will begin in Dublin, Paris and London, Macklemore said in an Instagram post. US dates and additional performers will be announced later, he said, adding that proceeds would be donated to organisations that support the Palestinian people.

"Being apolitical during a genocide doesn't work anymore," he said. "People are asking artists to show up, educate themselves and be in community. To use the stage for more than entertainment. To push back when the call for a Free Palestine is met with attempts to silence it." 

"A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: 'Free Palestine,'" he said on stage.

Macklemore said owners of stadiums where Sheeran was set to play had objected to those remarks.

Macklemore has ⁠been an outspoken critic of Israel's assault on Gaza and its occupation of the West Bank.

"If these last couple of weeks have shown us anything, it's that something has shifted over the last three years," Macklemore said on Thursday. "There has been a collective awakening around Palestinian liberation, the power of billionaires that try to censor that call, and what we expect from artists right now."

"What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage," he added. "When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which ones are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention."

What led to Macklemore’s removal?

It started when Macklemore, wearing a keffiyeh, performed in front of more than 80,000 people at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey earlier this month, speaking openly in support of Palestinians while singing his pro-Palestine anthem "Hind's Hall".

American Israeli lobby groups then launched a petition to pressure Sheeran to drop Macklemore as his opening act from future tour dates.

The rapper made a public statement last week on social media, announcing that he had been removed from Sheeran's tour due to an ultimatum from the pro-Israel billionaire and owner of the Gillette Stadium, Robert Kraft. 

Pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft led campaign to drop Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour
Read More »

"After my family, there is nothing I'm more passionate about than the State of Israel and my Jewish identity," Kraft said in Israel in 2019.

Macklemore's announcement not only drew huge support from fans and the international community, but also led all the opening acts on Sheeran's Loop Tour to withdraw in support of the rapper and the Palestinian people.

Among them were Finneas, a Grammy-winning musician and brother of singer Billie Eilish; the Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga; and the Danish band Lukas Graham.

"Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed," Finneas wrote on Instagram last Tuesday, adding: "I stand with Palestine and its people."

In the days that followed, Macklemore said he would donate the entire $1m he earned from the previous concerts of Sheeran's Loop Tour to six organisations supporting Palestinians.

Following his pledge, children's YouTube creator Ms Rachel announced she would also donate $1m to the Palestine Children's Relief Fund.

"I will match Macklemore's donation, and I invite every wealthy white celebrity to match it and speak out against the genocide in Gaza," she said.

item.description:
The Atlantic: Egypt's intelligence chief had warned Israel of Hamas attack

Days before Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel, Egypt's former intelligence chief Abbas Kamel delivered a blunt warning to senior Israeli officials at Ben Gurion Airport: "If you don't change course, Gaza is going to blow up in your faces," The Atlantic reported.

Kamel's warning first came to the fore when an Egyptian intelligence official told the Associated Press that Israel ignored repeated warnings that Hamas was planning “something big.” 

The Ynet news site also reported that the intelligence chief personally warned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 10 days before the attack that prompted Israel's ongoing genocidal onslaught on Gaza.

The Atlantic reported that Kamel didn’t provide Israeli officials with a date or specific information on the attack, and it was also not clear exactly with whom he met.

The magazine reported that the Egyptian plane, in which Kamel landed at the airport, remained on the ground in Israel for 67 minutes, according to an Israeli airport authority flight log, before returning to Cairo. 

An investigation published by Haaretz recently said the president of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) warned Israel's prime minister weeks before the 7 October attacks that Hamas was planning a major operation. Still, the Israeli premier dismissed the warning and did not inform Israel's security or military leaders. 

The warning was reportedly made during a 45-minute phone call, Haaretz reported.

"The emir explained that, in his assessment, [Hamas leader Yahya] Sinwar was preparing for a major event," a Gaza-born adviser to the UAE ruler, who was present during the call, said.

Report: Trump rejects Iran's ceasefire proposal, may resume bombing after midterms

President Trump has rejected Iran’s proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Citing officials, the newspaper reported that Trump is reluctant to resume major combat operations, while noting his views could change and that he could also end up being swayed by the midterm results.

Tehran’s proposal would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz and resumed nuclear talks in return for the US lifting its blockade of Iranian ports, which is causing serious damage to the country’s economy.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Amnesty stages 'End Genocide' protest at Austria-Israel Nations League match
item.description:
Amnesty stages 'End Genocide' protest at Austria-Israel Nations League match

Amnesty International Austria displayed a banner reading "End Genoice" inside the stadium in Linz on Thursday night as Austria faced Israel in the opening group match of the men's Uefa Nations League.

The protest renewed Amnesty's call for Uefa and Fifa to suspend the Israel Football Association (IFA) over "clear evidence" it continues to support illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories.

"Our protest is directed against many governments and sporting authorities that know exactly what is happening in the Gaza Strip and still do nothing to stand against genocide," said Alexander Weihrauch, a campaigner at Amnesty International Austria.

Weihrauch said Israel's "ongoing genocide" in Gaza, its "system of apartheid" against Palestinians, and the "ethnic cleansing in Area C" of the West Bank "must not disappear from public attention."

Amnesty first urged Fifa and Uefa in October 2025 to suspend the IFA unless settlement-based clubs were excluded from Israeli leagues. Fifa rejected that call in March 2026.

Amnesty is also pressing Austria and other EU states to suspend the EU-Israel Association Agreement and ban trade with implicated settlement entities.

Trump tries to dominate at the UN as his approval ratings plummet and even some Republicans stray from the script

Donald Trump stood before the United Nations on Tuesday and threatened to “annihilate” Iran. Yet even as the most powerful man on the planet flexed his military muscles, he was powerless to keep the gravitational pull of domestic politics at bay.

Heading into the UN building in New York, the US president was questioned by Kaitlan Collins, an anchor at CNN, which he had banned from the White House before a judge ruled against him. “I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me,” the 80-year-old snapped. “You should not be here covering me.”

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] UN expands list of companies operating in West Bank settlements
item.description:
UN expands list of companies operating in West Bank settlements

The United Nations human rights office issued a list on Friday adding 61 more companies operating in Israeli West Bank settlements, which the global body considers illegal.

The database is highly sensitive as firms could be targeted for boycotts or divestment to pressure Israel over settler expansion in the territory that is home to over 3 million Palestinians.

The database, first released in 2020, now includes 214 firms, mostly from Israel, but also from 10 other countries including France, Germany, China and the US. 

Newly added firms included Israeli pesticides maker ADAMA, part of Chinese-owned Syngenta Group, Israel-based real estate investment holding company Alony Hetz and Spain's Salvat Logistica.

They did not immediately respond to a request for comment on their inclusion in the UN database.

They joined companies such as travel agency Expedia and home-rental company Airbnb already on the list. 

Report by Reuters

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Morning recap
item.description:
Morning recap

Good morning Middle East Eye readers,

If you're just joining us, here are key developments:

•    Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran had presented the United States with a “concrete” seven-day plan and that the choice now rested with Washington.

•    The United States is having positive, constructive discussions with Iran through mediators and continues to discuss nuclear issues, a US official said on Friday when asked about Iran's proposed seven-day plan.

•    Oman’s Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi and his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi have discussed regional developments and efforts to ensure safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

•    President Trump has rejected Iran’s proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the November midterms, The Wall Street Journal reported.

•    Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has said that his country would allow UN nuclear inspectors into the country.

•    The Saudi Arabia-led coalition forces in Yemen said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Iran-backed Houthis towards the kingdom.

•    Yemen's government forces say they have made advances in the southern Taiz governorate, taking control of several areas and higher ground, according to Al Jazeera.

•    The United Nations human rights office issued a list on Friday adding 61 more companies operating in Israeli West Bank settlements, which the global body considers illegal.

•    Deputy prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, Nazhat Shameem Khan, has said that the court has insulated itself against potential court-wide sanctions from the US, according to the Financial Times.

•    Six Palestinians were arrested by Israeli forces across the occupied West Bank, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

•    Forty-one US lawmakers have called on Secretary of State Mark Rubio to press Israel for the release of Palestinian healthcare workers.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Trump labels Strait of Hormuz ‘Trump Strait’ in social media post
item.description:
Trump labels Strait of Hormuz ‘Trump Strait’ in social media post

US President Donald Trump has posted an image on his Truth Social platform showing the Strait of Hormuz circled and labelled “Trump Strait”, hours after Iran said it had presented a seven-day plan to reopen the strategic waterway.

The post came after The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump had rejected Iran’s proposal, citing unnamed US officials.

The report said Trump was sceptical that Tehran would meet his demands and believed a renewed US bombing campaign was likely.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran had presented the United States with a “concrete” seven-day plan and that the decision now rested with Washington.

US officials told Al Jazeera that Washington was in no hurry to respond to Iran’s proposal.
